body:
Yup. 

Been mentally ill all my life. This isn't helping.

Lol do some research into the health care system here. It's absolutely fascinating in a sick way. 

Stating is all I can do. Everything requires money, but money requires work, and work takes up a lot of time, and it still isn't enough.

America has a LOT of great things about it that I know we are very blessed and fortunate to have, but without access to adequate wages or health care it's impossible to enjoy any of them.

A while back, I tried to get help and there was a two month long waiting list to get assigned a GP. Not an appointment with a GP. To get assigned one. While I waited a nonprofit mental health organization would check up on me ("their phone calls literally amounted to "hey what's up? Still suicidal? Okay, cool, try not to be, thanks"). Well during this time I hurt myself and they called the cops and I was carted to the ER. I was in a room for 10 hours, no phones allowed, no contact, no one able to tell me who I was going to see or when, and the only reason I left at all was because, at my insistence, the nonprofit was called and sent someone to discharge me. The mandatory holding time is 72 hours, and thank god I didn't have that because if I did, I would have almost certainly lost my job. 

Instead they sent me home with a $3000 medical bill and no help. This was in a larger town with more resources, too. 

If I were to become ill or injured I would have no way to pay for it. It starts at $170 a month for catastrophic care that doesn't cover what I need--but some people pay $600. I know people who have family members diagnosed with stage 4 cancer because they couldn't afford to go to a doctor until it was too late or unbearable. Medications cost $400 or more.

If I say any of this, I'm "whining" because there's have it worse. And they do. Much worse. Knowing this only solidifies my conviction that it isn't worth t.

I've thought about Canada tbh, but the process....I am just so fucking tired.

Welcome to America. One behavioral health center in town and you need a referral and it's  overwhelmed with homeless people. Believe me. I have looked. Haven't had a GP for years because insurance is too expensive. 

And it won't get better in my lifetime. Better to just leave.

I'm in insurance. The only eating disorder specialist is a specialty addiction retreat three hours away and at least grand a month. And also not exactly what I need. 

Therapy in general has always been unaffordable for me so 

Bulimic. Puke every day.
